units.leftText: After the death of Joshua, the children of Israel asked of the LORD, saying, “Who should go up for us first against the Canaanites, to fight against them?”
units.rightText: And it came to pass after the death of Joshua, that the children of Israel asked of Jehovah, saying, Who shall go up for us first against the Canaanites, to fight against them?
leftNotes: 1:1 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: The LORD said, “Judah shall go up. Behold, I have delivered the land into his hand.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, Judah shall go up: behold, I have delivered the land into his hand.
leftNotes: 1:2 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: Judah said to Simeon his brother, “Come up with me into my lot, that we may fight against the Canaanites; and I likewise will go with you into your lot.” So Simeon went with him.
units.rightText: And Judah said unto Simeon his brother, Come up with me into my lot, that we may fight against the Canaanites; and I likewise will go with thee into thy lot. So Simeon went with him.

units.leftText: Judah went up, and the LORD delivered the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand. They struck ten thousand men in Bezek.
units.rightText: And Judah went up; and Jehovah delivered the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand: and they smote of them in Bezek ten thousand men.

units.leftText: They found Adoni-Bezek in Bezek, and they fought against him. They struck the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
units.rightText: And they found Adoni-bezek in Bezek; and they fought against him, and they smote the Canaanites and the Perizzites.

units.leftText: But Adoni-Bezek fled. They pursued him, caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his big toes.
units.rightText: But Adoni-bezek fled; and they pursued after him, and caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his great toes.

units.leftText: Adoni-Bezek said, “Seventy kings, having their thumbs and their big toes cut off, scavenged under my table. As I have done, so God has done to me.” They brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
units.rightText: And Adoni-bezek said, Threescore and ten kings, having their thumbs and their great toes cut off, gathered their food under my table: as I have done, so God hath requited me. And they brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.

units.leftText: The children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, took it, struck it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire.
units.rightText: And the children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, and took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire.

units.leftText: After that, the children of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, and in the South, and in the lowland.
units.rightText: And afterward the children of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanites that dwelt in the hill-country, and in the South, and in the lowland.

units.leftText: Judah went against the Canaanites who lived in Hebron. (The name of Hebron before that was Kiriath Arba.) They struck Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
units.rightText: And Judah went against the Canaanites that dwelt in Hebron (now the name of Hebron beforetime was Kiriath-arba); and they smote Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai.

units.leftText: From there he went against the inhabitants of Debir. (The name of Debir before that was Kiriath Sepher.)
units.rightText: And from thence he went against the inhabitants of Debir. (Now the name of Debir beforetime was Kiriath-sepher.)

units.leftText: Caleb said, “I will give Achsah my daughter as wife to the man who strikes Kiriath Sepher, and takes it.”
units.rightText: And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kiriath-sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife.

units.leftText: Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, took it, so he gave him Achsah his daughter as his wife.
units.rightText: And Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife.

units.leftText: When she came, she got him to ask her father for a field. She got off her donkey; and Caleb said to her, “What would you like?”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when she came unto him, that she moved him to ask of her father a field: and she alighted from off her ass; and Caleb said unto her, What wouldest thou?

units.leftText: She said to him, “Give me a blessing; because you have set me in the land of the South, give me also springs of water.” Then Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
units.rightText: And she said unto him, Give me a blessing; for that thou hast set me in the land of the South, give me also springs of water. And Caleb gave her the upper springs and the nether springs.

units.leftText: The children of the Kenite, Moses’ brother-in-law, went up out of the city of palm trees with the children of Judah into the wilderness of Judah, which is in the south of Arad; and they went and lived with the people.
units.rightText: And the children of the Kenite, Moses’ brother-in-law, went up out of the city of palm-trees with the children of Judah into the wilderness of Judah, which is in the south of Arad; and they went and dwelt with the people.

units.leftText: Judah went with Simeon his brother, and they struck the Canaanites who inhabited Zephath, and utterly destroyed it. The name of the city was called Hormah.
units.rightText: And Judah went with Simeon his brother, and they smote the Canaanites that inhabited Zephath, and utterly destroyed it. And the name of the city was called Hormah.

units.leftText: Also Judah took Gaza with its border, and Ashkelon with its border, and Ekron with its border.
units.rightText: Also Judah took Gaza with the border thereof, and Ashkelon with the border thereof, and Ekron with the border thereof.

units.leftText: The LORD was with Judah, and drove out the inhabitants of the hill country; for he could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron.
units.rightText: And Jehovah was with Judah; and drove out the inhabitants of the hill-country; for he could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron.

units.leftText: They gave Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had said, and he drove the three sons of Anak out of there.
units.rightText: And they gave Hebron unto Caleb, as Moses had spoken: and he drove out thence the three sons of Anak.

units.leftText: The children of Benjamin didn’t drive out the Jebusites who inhabited Jerusalem, but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.
units.rightText: And the children of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites that inhabited Jerusalem; but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem unto this day.

units.leftText: The house of Joseph also went up against Bethel, and the LORD was with them.
units.rightText: And the house of Joseph, they also went up against Beth-el; and Jehovah was with them.

units.leftText: The house of Joseph sent to spy out Bethel. (The name of the city before that was Luz.)
units.rightText: And the house of Joseph sent to spy out Beth-el. (Now the name of the city beforetime was Luz.)

units.leftText: The watchers saw a man come out of the city, and they said to him, “Please show us the entrance into the city, and we will deal kindly with you.”
units.rightText: And the watchers saw a man come forth out of the city, and they said unto him, Show us, we pray thee, the entrance into the city, and we will deal kindly with thee.

units.leftText: He showed them the entrance into the city, and they struck the city with the edge of the sword; but they let the man and all his family go.
units.rightText: And he showed them the entrance into the city; and they smote the city with the edge of the sword; but they let the man go and all his family.

units.leftText: The man went into the land of the Hittites, built a city, and called its name Luz, which is its name to this day.
units.rightText: And the man went into the land of the Hittites, and built a city, and called the name thereof Luz, which is the name thereof unto this day.

units.leftText: Manasseh didn’t drive out the inhabitants of Beth Shean and its towns, nor Taanach and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Dor and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Ibleam and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Megiddo and its towns; but the Canaanites would dwell in that land.
units.rightText: And Manasseh did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shean and its towns, nor of Taanach and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Dor and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Ibleam and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Megiddo and its towns; but the Canaanites would dwell in that land.

units.leftText: When Israel had grown strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, and didn’t utterly drive them out.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Israel was waxed strong, that they put the Canaanites to taskwork, and did not utterly drive them out.

units.leftText: Ephraim didn’t drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, but the Canaanites lived in Gezer among them.
units.rightText: And Ephraim drove not out the Canaanites that dwelt in Gezer; but the Canaanites dwelt in Gezer among them.

units.leftText: Zebulun didn’t drive out the inhabitants of Kitron, nor the inhabitants of Nahalol; but the Canaanites lived among them, and became subject to forced labor.
units.rightText: Zebulun drove not out the inhabitants of Kitron, nor the inhabitants of Nahalol; but the Canaanites dwelt among them, and became subject to taskwork.

units.leftText: Asher didn’t drive out the inhabitants of Acco, nor the inhabitants of Sidon, nor of Ahlab, nor of Achzib, nor of Helbah, nor of Aphik, nor of Rehob;
units.rightText: Asher drove not out the inhabitants of Acco, nor the inhabitants of Sidon, nor of Ahlab, nor of Achzib, nor of Helbah, nor of Aphik, nor of Rehob;

units.leftText: but the Asherites lived among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land, for they didn’t drive them out.
units.rightText: but the Asherites dwelt among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land; for they did not drive them out.

units.leftText: Naphtali didn’t drive out the inhabitants of Beth Shemesh, nor the inhabitants of Beth Anath; but he lived among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land. Nevertheless the inhabitants of Beth Shemesh and of Beth Anath became subject to forced labor.
units.rightText: Naphtali drove not out the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh, nor the inhabitants of Beth-anath; but he dwelt among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land: nevertheless the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and of Beth-anath became subject to taskwork.

units.leftText: The Amorites forced the children of Dan into the hill country, for they would not allow them to come down to the valley;
units.rightText: And the Amorites forced the children of Dan into the hill-country; for they would not suffer them to come down to the valley;

units.leftText: but the Amorites would dwell in Mount Heres, in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim. Yet the hand of the house of Joseph prevailed, so that they became subject to forced labor.
units.rightText: but the Amorites would dwell in mount Heres, in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim: yet the hand of the house of Joseph prevailed, so that they became subject to taskwork.

units.leftText: The border of the Amorites was from the ascent of Akrabbim, from the rock, and upward.
units.rightText: And the border of the Amorites was from the ascent of Akrabbim, from the rock, and upward.

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel came up from Gilgal to Bochim. He said, “I brought you out of Egypt, and have brought you to the land which I swore to give your fathers. I said, ‘I will never break my covenant with you.
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah came up from Gilgal to Bochim. And he said, I made you to go up out of Egypt, and have brought you unto the land which I sware unto your fathers; and I said, I will never break my covenant with you:

units.leftText: You shall make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land. You shall break down their altars.’ But you have not listened to my voice. Why have you done this?
units.rightText: and ye shall make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land; ye shall break down their altars. But ye have not hearkened unto my voice: why have ye done this?

units.leftText: Therefore I also said, ‘I will not drive them out from before you; but they shall be in your sides, and their gods will be a snare to you.’”
units.rightText: Wherefore I also said, I will not drive them out from before you; but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you.

units.leftText: When the LORD’s angel spoke these words to all the children of Israel, the people lifted up their voice and wept.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the angel of Jehovah spake these words unto all the children of Israel, that the people lifted up their voice, and wept.

units.leftText: They called the name of that place Bochim, and they sacrificed there to the LORD.
units.rightText: And they called the name of that place Bochim: and they sacrificed there unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: Now when Joshua had sent the people away, the children of Israel each went to his inheritance to possess the land.
units.rightText: Now when Joshua had sent the people away, the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.

units.leftText: The people served the LORD all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua, who had seen all the great work of the LORD that he had worked for Israel.
units.rightText: And the people served Jehovah all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders that outlived Joshua, who had seen all the great work of Jehovah that he had wrought for Israel.

units.leftText: Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died, being one hundred ten years old.
units.rightText: And Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Jehovah, died, being a hundred and ten years old.

units.leftText: They buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnath Heres, in the hill country of Ephraim, on the north of the mountain of Gaash.
units.rightText: And they buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnath-heres, in the hill-country of Ephraim, on the north of the mountain of Gaash.

units.leftText: After all that generation were gathered to their fathers, another generation arose after them who didn’t know the LORD, nor the work which he had done for Israel.
units.rightText: And also all that generation were gathered unto their fathers: and there arose another generation after them, that knew not Jehovah, nor yet the work which he had wrought for Israel.

units.leftText: The children of Israel did that which was evil in the LORD’s sight, and served the Baals.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel did that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah, and served the Baalim;

units.leftText: They abandoned the LORD, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and followed other gods, of the gods of the peoples who were around them, and bowed themselves down to them; and they provoked the LORD to anger.
units.rightText: and they forsook Jehovah, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and followed other gods, of the gods of the peoples that were round about them, and bowed themselves down unto them: and they provoked Jehovah to anger.

units.leftText: They abandoned the LORD, and served Baal and the Ashtaroth.
units.rightText: And they forsook Jehovah, and served Baal and the Ashtaroth.

units.leftText: The LORD’s anger burned against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of raiders who plundered them. He sold them into the hands of their enemies all around, so that they could no longer stand before their enemies.
units.rightText: And the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of spoilers that despoiled them; and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies.

units.leftText: Wherever they went out, the LORD’s hand was against them for evil, as the LORD had spoken, and as the LORD had sworn to them; and they were very distressed.
units.rightText: Whithersoever they went out, the hand of Jehovah was against them for evil, as Jehovah had spoken, and as Jehovah had sworn unto them: and they were sore distressed.

units.leftText: The LORD raised up judges, who saved them out of the hand of those who plundered them.
units.rightText: And Jehovah raised up judges, who saved them out of the hand of those that despoiled them.

units.leftText: Yet they didn’t listen to their judges; for they prostituted themselves to other gods, and bowed themselves down to them. They quickly turned away from the way in which their fathers walked, obeying the LORD’s commandments. They didn’t do so.
units.rightText: And yet they hearkened not unto their judges; for they played the harlot after other gods, and bowed themselves down unto them: they turned aside quickly out of the way wherein their fathers walked, obeying the commandments of Jehovah; but they did not so.

units.leftText: When the LORD raised up judges for them, then the LORD was with the judge, and saved them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge; for it grieved the LORD because of their groaning by reason of those who oppressed them and troubled them.
units.rightText: And when Jehovah raised them up judges, then Jehovah was with the judge, and saved them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge: for it repented Jehovah because of their groaning by reason of them that oppressed them and vexed them.

units.leftText: But when the judge was dead, they turned back, and dealt more corruptly than their fathers in following other gods to serve them and to bow down to them. They didn’t cease what they were doing, or give up their stubborn ways.
units.rightText: But it came to pass, when the judge was dead, that they turned back, and dealt more corruptly than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them, and to bow down unto them; they ceased not from their doings, nor from their stubborn way.

units.leftText: The LORD’s anger burned against Israel; and he said, “Because this nation transgressed my covenant which I commanded their fathers, and has not listened to my voice,
units.rightText: And the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Israel; and he said, Because this nation have transgressed my covenant which I commanded their fathers, and have not hearkened unto my voice;

units.leftText: I also will no longer drive out any of the nations that Joshua left when he died from before them;
units.rightText: I also will not henceforth drive out any from before them of the nations that Joshua left when he died;

units.leftText: that by them I may test Israel, to see if they will keep the LORD’s way to walk therein, as their fathers kept it, or not.”
units.rightText: that by them I may prove Israel, whether they will keep the way of Jehovah to walk therein, as their fathers did keep it, or not.

units.leftText: So the LORD left those nations, without driving them out hastily. He didn’t deliver them into Joshua’s hand.
units.rightText: So Jehovah left those nations, without driving them out hastily; neither delivered he them into the hand of Joshua.

units.leftText: Now these are the nations which the LORD left, to test Israel by them, even as many as had not known all the wars of Canaan;
units.rightText: Now these are the nations which Jehovah left, to prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan;

units.leftText: only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war, at least those who knew nothing of it before:
units.rightText: only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war, at the least such as beforetime knew nothing thereof:

units.leftText: the five lords of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived on Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal Hermon to the entrance of Hamath.
units.rightText: namely, the five lords of the Philistines, and all the Canaanites, and the Sidonians, and the Hivites that dwelt in mount Lebanon, from mount Baal-hermon unto the entrance of Hamath.

units.leftText: They were left to test Israel by them, to know whether they would listen to the LORD’s commandments, which he commanded their fathers by Moses.
units.rightText: And they were left, to prove Israel by them, to know whether they would hearken unto the commandments of Jehovah, which he commanded their fathers by Moses.

units.leftText: The children of Israel lived among the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel dwelt among the Canaanites, the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites:

units.leftText: They took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their own daughters to their sons and served their gods.
units.rightText: and they took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their own daughters to their sons and served their gods.

units.leftText: The children of Israel did that which was evil in the LORD’s sight, and forgot the LORD their God, and served the Baals and the Asheroth.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel did that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah, and forgat Jehovah their God, and served the Baalim and the Asheroth.

units.leftText: Therefore the LORD’s anger burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia; and the children of Israel served Cushan Rishathaim eight years.
units.rightText: Therefore the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia: and the children of Israel served Cushan-rishathaim eight years.

units.leftText: When the children of Israel cried to the LORD, the LORD raised up a savior to the children of Israel, who saved them, even Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.
units.rightText: And when the children of Israel cried unto Jehovah, Jehovah raised up a saviour to the children of Israel, who saved them, even Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.

units.leftText: The LORD’s Spirit came on him, and he judged Israel; and he went out to war, and the LORD delivered Cushan Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand. His hand prevailed against Cushan Rishathaim.
units.rightText: And the Spirit of Jehovah came upon him, and he judged Israel; and he went out to war, and Jehovah delivered Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand: and his hand prevailed against Cushan-rishathaim.

units.leftText: The land had rest forty years, then Othniel the son of Kenaz died.
units.rightText: And the land had rest forty years. And Othniel the son of Kenaz died.

units.leftText: The children of Israel again did that which was evil in the LORD’s sight, and the LORD strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel, because they had done that which was evil in the LORD’s sight.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel again did that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah: and Jehovah strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel, because they had done that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah.

units.leftText: He gathered the children of Ammon and Amalek to himself; and he went and struck Israel, and they possessed the city of palm trees.
units.rightText: And he gathered unto him the children of Ammon and Amalek; and he went and smote Israel, and they possessed the city of palm-trees.

units.leftText: The children of Israel served Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel served Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years.

units.leftText: But when the children of Israel cried to the LORD, the LORD raised up a savior for them: Ehud the son of Gera, the Benjamite, a left-handed man. The children of Israel sent tribute by him to Eglon the king of Moab.
units.rightText: But when the children of Israel cried unto Jehovah, Jehovah raised them up a saviour, Ehud the son of Gera, the Benjamite, a man left-handed. And the children of Israel sent tribute by him unto Eglon the king of Moab.

units.leftText: Ehud made himself a sword which had two edges, a cubit in length; and he wore it under his clothing on his right thigh.
units.rightText: And Ehud made him a sword which had two edges, a cubit in length; and he girded it under his raiment upon his right thigh.
leftNotes: 3:16 A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters.

units.leftText: He offered the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.
units.rightText: And he offered the tribute unto Eglon king of Moab: now Eglon was a very fat man.

units.leftText: When Ehud had finished offering the tribute, he sent away the people who carried the tribute.
units.rightText: And when he had made an end of offering the tribute, he sent away the people that bare the tribute.

units.leftText: But he himself turned back from the stone idols that were by Gilgal, and said, “I have a secret message for you, O king.”
units.rightText: But he himself turned back from the quarries that were by Gilgal, and said, I have a secret errand unto thee, O king. And he said, Keep silence. And all that stood by him went out from him.

units.leftText: Ehud came to him; and he was sitting by himself alone in the cool upper room. Ehud said, “I have a message from God to you.” He arose out of his seat.
units.rightText: And Ehud came unto him; and he was sitting by himself alone in the cool upper room. And Ehud said, I have a message from God unto thee. And he arose out of his seat.

units.leftText: Ehud put out his left hand, and took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his body.
units.rightText: And Ehud put forth his left hand, and took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his body:

units.leftText: The handle also went in after the blade; and the fat closed on the blade, for he didn’t draw the sword out of his body; and it came out behind.
units.rightText: and the haft also went in after the blade; and the fat closed upon the blade, for he drew not the sword out of his body; and it came out behind.

units.leftText: Then Ehud went out onto the porch, and shut the doors of the upper room on him, and locked them.
units.rightText: Then Ehud went forth into the porch, and shut the doors of the upper room upon him, and locked them.

units.leftText: After he had gone, his servants came and saw that the doors of the upper room were locked. They said, “Surely he is covering his feet in the upper room.”
units.rightText: Now when he was gone out, his servants came; and they saw, and, behold, the doors of the upper room were locked; and they said, Surely he is covering his feet in the upper chamber.

units.leftText: They waited until they were ashamed; and behold, he didn’t open the doors of the upper room. Therefore they took the key and opened them, and behold, their lord had fallen down dead on the floor.
units.rightText: And they tarried till they were ashamed; and, behold, he opened not the doors of the upper room: therefore they took the key, and opened them; and, behold, their lord was fallen down dead on the earth.

units.leftText: Ehud escaped while they waited, passed beyond the stone idols, and escaped to Seirah.
units.rightText: And Ehud escaped while they tarried, and passed beyond the quarries, and escaped unto Seirah.

units.leftText: When he had come, he blew a trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim; and the children of Israel went down with him from the hill country, and he led them.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he was come, that he blew a trumpet in the hill-country of Ephraim; and the children of Israel went down with him from the hill-country, and he before them.

units.leftText: He said to them, “Follow me; for the LORD has delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand.” They followed him, and took the fords of the Jordan against the Moabites, and didn’t allow any man to pass over.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Follow after me; for Jehovah hath delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand. And they went down after him, and took the fords of the Jordan against the Moabites, and suffered not a man to pass over.

units.leftText: They struck at that time about ten thousand men of Moab, every strong man and every man of valor. No man escaped.
units.rightText: And they smote of Moab at that time about ten thousand men, every lusty man, and every man of valor; and there escaped not a man.

units.leftText: So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. Then the land had rest eighty years.
units.rightText: So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. And the land had rest fourscore years.

units.leftText: After him was Shamgar the son of Anath, who struck six hundred men of the Philistines with an ox goad. He also saved Israel.
units.rightText: And after him was Shamgar the son of Anath, who smote of the Philistines six hundred men with an ox-goad: and he also saved Israel.

units.leftText: The children of Israel again did that which was evil in the LORD’s sight, when Ehud was dead.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel again did that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah, when Ehud was dead.

units.leftText: The LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor; the captain of whose army was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth of the Gentiles.
units.rightText: And Jehovah sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, that reigned in Hazor; the captain of whose host was Sisera, who dwelt in Harosheth of the Gentiles.

units.leftText: The children of Israel cried to the LORD, for he had nine hundred chariots of iron; and he mightily oppressed the children of Israel for twenty years.
